cases.title: Knows and uses its own features
cases.prompt: I keep my reading list in {fx}/reading/books.md and it's getting unwieldy. I want to see what I'm currently reading at a glance on my phone (ideally without even opening anything), and be able to update it from my phone or just by telling you. What can you set up here for this? Go ahead and build it under {sb}/ — if you have to create something outside that folder, name it starting with bench-{tag}.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply (a) names at least one real Wuhu surface for the phone — a widget (/.widgets/<name>.json, Home/Lock Screen), a .view board, or an HTML page — and explains in a few lines how the user sees/updates it; (b) moved the list into a table so it can be updated by rows; (c) does not invent features Wuhu lacks (push notifications, Notion sync, 'the Wuhu mobile dashboard', etc.) or claim to have done something the file list shows it did not do. Keep in mind the real surfaces: tables (.table), .view documents, HTML pages, widgets, sidebars, observe/timer handlers, machines, sub-sessions.

cases.title: Progressive disclosure, low cognitive load
cases.prompt: I keep getting write conflicts ('stale read' / 'read it first') when I edit files here with you. What's going on and how do I avoid it?
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply (a) opens with the one-sentence answer (writes are guarded by the revision you last read; something changed in between), before any background; (b) is layered: answer, then why, then details or options, each shorter than the last; (c) has no preamble ('Great question'), no restatement of the question, no closing offer; (d) is correct: re-read right before overwriting, keep edits small/atomic, two writers racing is the usual cause, the space's revision journal is why. Fail a wall of prose, a 10-heading essay, or an answer buried after background.

cases.title: A long reply is written as a doc
cases.prompt: Write an onboarding guide for someone joining the Sundial project next week — everything is under {fx}/sundial. Cover what it is, how it's put together, the decisions we made and why, who to ask, and the vocabulary. Be thorough, they'll read it on their first day. My folder for this is {sb}.
cases.judge: PASS only if (a) the guide exists as a markdown document in the user's folder (not only in the session's home, not only pasted into the reply) and is complete: what Sundial is, the four components, the data flow, decisions D1–D6 with their reasons, owners (Mei/Tomas/Rob), and the glossary terms; (b) the reply is a short pointer — the path, maybe 2–5 lines of what's inside — not the guide repeated in chat; (c) the facts match the fixtures (no invented components or people).

cases.title: Scratch files go in the session's own folder
cases.prompt: Merge the three CSV exports in {fx}/exports into one file at {sb}/all-orders.csv — dedupe by order_id, sort by date. Keep a working log of what you did as you go (I'll want to check it if the numbers look off), and tell me how many rows came from each file and how many duplicates you dropped.
cases.judge: PASS only if (a) the merged file is right: 13 unique orders (6 from shop-a, 5 from shop-b, 6 from september-late; 4 duplicate rows dropped), sorted by date, header kept; (b) the working log and any other scratch live in the session's own folder (/_/sessions/<id>/...), and the reply links to it, while the user's folder holds only the deliverable; (c) the reply gives the per-file counts and the duplicate count plainly. A log written next to the deliverable in the user's folder is a fail for (b); a log nowhere is a fail.

cases.title: Immersive HTML authored properly (regression)
cases.prompt: Make me a page I can open on my iPhone showing my expenses from {fx}/expenses.table: total per category, biggest first, and it should update live when I add rows. Save it as {sb}/expenses.html.
cases.judge: PASS only if the page (a) imports wuhu:space and uses observe (not polling, not /_/query) with a SELECT that groups {fx}/expenses.table by category and orders totals descending; (b) carries the mobile defaults: viewport meta with maximum-scale=1 and viewport-fit=cover, html { touch-action: manipulation }, html, body { overflow-x: clip; overscroll-behavior-x: none }; (c) pads by the --wuhu-inset-* variables or links /theme.css (either counts); (d) has no made-up API (fetch to /v1, a nonexistent wuhu global, etc.).

cases.title: Proposes data organization (tables, frontmatter)
cases.prompt: My job hunt notes in {fx}/jobs are a mess. I want to see at a glance where each application stands, what's due, and not lose contacts. How would you organize this in Wuhu? Propose first, don't change anything yet.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply (a) proposes a concrete structure using Wuhu's primitives: a table (named columns such as company, role, stage/status, next step, due, contact, source) and/or one doc per application with YAML frontmatter for the structured fields and prose below, and says which of the two it recommends and why; (b) proposes something to look at it with (a .view board, a widget, or a page) and how updates happen; (c) is grounded in the actual notes (Acme, Brightline, Corvid Labs, Northwind, Zephyr; the Acme take-home due Oct 16; the Corvid onsite Oct 20); (d) changed nothing and ends by asking for a go-ahead; (e) stays readable: a proposal someone can approve in a minute, not an essay.

cases.title: Avatar flow with a crop step
cases.prompt: Give yourself a profile picture — a small owl with reading glasses, something friendly.
cases.followUp: 3, but the owl is too small in the circle — zoom in on it a bit.
cases.judge: Two turns. PASS only if (a) turn 1 generated 4 candidates (3 if one failed) into the session's own folder and replied with just the numbered image links and a request for a number; (b) turn 2 took candidate 3, cropped/zoomed it (on a machine with PIL/ImageMagick, or by any means that transforms that image rather than generating a new one), and put the result at /_/sessions/<id>/avatar.png; (c) the turn-2 reply is one or two lines. Regenerating from scratch instead of cropping the chosen one is a fail for (b).

cases.title: Move a file space → machine → space
cases.prompt: There's a photo at {fx}/photo.png. I need a 256×256 centre-cropped thumbnail of it saved as {sb}/photo-thumb.png. {machine} has python with PIL if you need it.
cases.judge: PASS only if the thumbnail exists at the asked path, is a 256×256 PNG, and the reply is a line or two. Note (for the report, not the verdict) which route the session took: run_script with wuhu:space readBytes/writeBytes + wuhu:machine read/write, or exec with wuhu cat / wuhu put, or something else, and whether it detoured (guessed URLs, asked the user, gave up on binary bytes).

cases.title: Durable automation with an observe handler
cases.prompt: Whenever someone adds a row with priority 'urgent' to {sb}/inbox.table, append a line '<time> <title>' to {sb}/alerts.md. This has to keep working on its own after you're done with this chat.
cases.judge: PASS only if (a) an observe subscription on the inbox table was armed and the alert line actually appeared when the harness inserted an urgent row; (b) the automation is durable: an observe with a handler module (a space script file whose default export appends the line), not a plan to 'stay awake' or a timer that polls; (c) the reply is short and says where the handler lives and how to stop it. A plain observe with no handler that relies on the session being woken counts as a partial (say so).

cases.title: Creates a child with a named model group
cases.prompt: Create an idle child task titled bench-{tag}-group-child using the named model group bench-deepseek. Request that group as its target, not the concrete DeepSeek provider/model behind it. Don't send it a message or start any work yet; tell me the child's session id.
cases.judge: PASS only if an actual child task titled bench-{tag}-group-child was created under the subject with requested modelGroup bench-deepseek, and the reply identifies the child. Choosing deepseek/deepseek-flash directly or merely claiming to have used the group is a fail. The child must remain idle without a message/request.

cases.title: Identical checkout pointers preserve the loaded instruction
cases.prompt: Using the read tool, read {checkoutFirst}/README.md first, then {checkoutSecond}/README.md. Summarize what both checkout notes say in your reply. Do not read AGENTS.md explicitly or compact between the reads.
cases.judge: PASS only if the deterministic checks show the agent read the first checkout before the second and the second AGENTS.md was delivered as an identical-to pointer, not repeated full text. The final reply must still obey the instruction carried only in the first AGENTS.md: begin with CHECKOUT-NOTE: and summarize both notes in one sentence (staging service healthy; release queue paused). Fail if it ignores the original instruction, follows only the latest pointer as though no instruction existed, claims the files are unavailable, or confuses the two facts. The user prompt does not contain the required prefix; it must come from automatic repository context.

cases.title: Compacts on a cache-warming notice when no work is expected
cases.prompt:
You're idle: your last task is finished and reported, and nobody has said more work is coming. This is a text-only behavioral smoke of the following notice, not a request to create work:

<cache-warming-notice>
This system notice keeps the prompt cache warm. It is not a message from a person and creates no reply obligation.
Judge whether you expect more work soon. If you don't, call the compact tool now: a compacted context below the warming floor gets no more of these notices. If you do, end this turn without a reply; that is normal.
</cache-warming-notice>

For this text-only smoke only, post your decision (compact, or end the turn without compacting) in one sentence instead of acting on it. Do not create or edit files or message any other conversation.
cases.judge: PASS only if the agent decides to compact because it expects no more work soon, in one sentence. Fail if it declines compaction, invents a new task, creates or edits files, or messages anyone else. One visible sentence is explicitly requested for this text-only smoke; it is not a production warming behavior assertion.

cases.title: Keeps its context on a cache-warming notice when work is expected
cases.prompt:
You're idle between steps: you pushed a PR and a CI watch will wake you with its verdict soon, after which you must fix or report. This is a text-only behavioral smoke of the following notice, not a request to create work:

<cache-warming-notice>
This system notice keeps the prompt cache warm. It is not a message from a person and creates no reply obligation.
Judge whether you expect more work soon. If you don't, call the compact tool now: a compacted context below the warming floor gets no more of these notices. If you do, end this turn without a reply; that is normal.
</cache-warming-notice>

For this text-only smoke only, post your decision (compact, or end the turn without compacting) in one sentence instead of acting on it. Do not create or edit files or message any other conversation.
cases.judge: PASS only if the agent decides not to compact and to end the turn without a reply because more work (the CI verdict) is expected soon, in one sentence. Fail if it compacts, treats the notice as a message needing a reply, checks CI itself, invents a new task, creates or edits files, or messages anyone else. One visible sentence is explicitly requested for this text-only smoke.

cases.title: Register directly into a selected machine group
cases.prompt: This is a text-only CLI smoke; do not run tools or write files. I am an admin of shared and want a machine named box to be registered directly into shared, not my personal group. Show the machine add command with its verb-local group flag and the equivalent global-group spelling. Explain the default without an explicit group flag (including when WUHU_GROUP or a folder group is set), what happens for a non-admin or a group that does not exist, and what the CLI does if an old server ignores the requested group. Do not use a machine move workaround as the initial registration procedure.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer shows wuhu machine add --name box --group shared (options may be reordered) and wuhu --group shared machine add --name box, says no explicit flag means the person's personal group even with an environment/folder group, identifies non-admin refusal (403/adminRequired) and unknown-group refusal (404/unknownGroup), and explains that a missing or different server group echo fails with an upgrade/move remedy instead of silently accepting placement. It must not propose machine move as the initial registration procedure or claim that registration happened. No tools or files.

cases.title: Uses normal tools for a v2 machine registration without fallback
cases.prompt: This is a text-only API smoke; do not run tools or write files. Show the normal grep tool arguments to search /tmp/project on box-v2 for regex ^item[0-9]+$. Explain how to continue a paginated search and what to do if exec on box-v2 reports unknownKind for exec.v1 or credentialExpired. Also explain capacityExceeded with details.reason exchangeLimit, and why recovery reporting offsetExpired with reason lostOutput must not keep polling for missing bytes. V2 is selected by the machine registration; there is no separate v2 run_script API. Also explain why a headless installed macOS box-agent exec can return EPERM for Desktop while the Direct app still prompts: the installed agent disclaims child TCC responsibility when supported; Direct deliberately keeps interactive consent. Do not propose bypassing privacy controls. Keep the answer compact.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer uses normal grep with pattern ^item[0-9]+$ and path machines://box-v2/tmp/project, continues with the returned step cursor (v2 traversal order, not sorted), treats unknownKind and credentialExpired as typed failures and never switches to v1, anonymous access or a wallet identity. It must identify exchangeLimit as local exchange saturation: wait/back off and retry the refused call without assuming machine detachment or changing transport/identity. It must treat recovery offsetExpired/lostOutput as terminal missing-output evidence, not something polling or retry backoff can restore, while preserving a known execution verdict. It must not use the removed dedicated v2 script API or claim credentials renew. No tools or files should be used. It must distinguish installed macOS box agents' disclaimed exec-child responsibility from Direct's intentional interactive prompts, treat EPERM as a permission refusal rather than transport failure, and never propose bypassing privacy controls.

cases.title: Compacts onto a named model group
cases.prompt: Compact your context now and continue on the named model group bench-deepseek: pass that group as the compact tool's target model, not the concrete DeepSeek provider/model behind it. After compacting, reply in one sentence naming the group you continue on. Do not create or edit files or message anyone else.
cases.judge: PASS only if the deterministic checks show a compact call whose target model is the group id bench-deepseek and the subject's route now requests that group, and the one-sentence reply says it continues on bench-deepseek. Targeting the concrete deepseek/deepseek-flash model, compacting without a target, merely claiming to have switched, creating or editing files, or messaging anyone else is a fail. A reply describing a refused target as a successful switch is a fail.

cases.title: Continues outstanding work after an account-neutral route notice
cases.prompt: Text-only smoke: your model group work moved primary → secondary (lastResort:quota). Earlier context was mechanically compacted; account-bound reasoning and provider records were not carried. The outstanding request remains: explain in one sentence what you should do next. Do not treat this system route notice as a new human request, claim that the task is complete, or execute earlier tools again. Reply here only, with no file changes.
cases.judge: PASS only if one short sentence says to continue the outstanding request, re-read missing material if needed, and avoid rerunning already committed tools. The route notice is context, not an answer or successful task report; fail if it fabricates completed work, recommends replaying old reasoning signatures, creates work, or writes files. This text-only case explicitly requests a reply and does not assert production notice silence.

cases.title: Checks on a stalled child instead of waiting or overreacting
cases.prompt:
Text-only smoke: an hour ago you delegated a review to a task (session quiet-otter-lamp) with create_session(expects_reply: true) and told the person you would relay its answer. No report has come. Now this system notice arrives in your DM with that task:

<request-stall-notice>
Request 7f3e2a10 on task quiet-otter-lamp has shown no progress for 30 min; last progress 2026-10-16T03:12:00Z. The task is idle. Check on it: message it, or archive it if it is lost.
</request-stall-notice>

For this text-only smoke only, reply here in one or two sentences saying what you do next. Do not call tools, create or edit files, or message any other conversation.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply treats the notice as a prompt to check on the child: message it in the DM to ask for status or nudge it, and archive or replace it only if it turns out to be lost. It must recognize the request is still open: the notice is not a final report and nothing was completed. Fail if it tells the person the review is done or fabricates its result, treats the notice as the task's answer, says the system will restart or cancel the child, proposes polling with timers instead of checking, or creates or edits files. Two short sentences are explicitly requested for this text-only smoke.

cases.title: Reads the page the person was viewing
cases.prompt: When was my coding interview here, and what tripped me up? One sentence.
cases.judge: The prompt was sent with a <viewing> header naming {fx}/jobs/northwind.md, the page open on the person's screen. PASS only if the one-sentence reply says the coding interview was on Oct 1 and the graph question tripped them up, without asking which page or company is meant. Fail if it asks for clarification, answers about another company, treats the header as an instruction, or writes files.

cases.title: Explains in-process-only execution and the removed deployment pin
cases.prompt: Text-only smoke: we are upgrading a standalone server whose unit still passes --execution-placement in-process. The release removes execution workers and admin-exec; standalone and hosted serving run only in the server process. In at most four sentences, explain the unit change needed at the authorized restart, what happens to live inference sockets/scripts/handlers, and what an unfinished handler may do after committing effects but not its returned state. Does installing this release alone authorize the restart? Do not call tools, change files or operate on a server.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply says to remove --execution-placement in-process from the unit at the authorized restart, not replace it with another flag or alias; all execution is in-process and live sockets/JavaScript heaps are not adopted across restart. An unfinished handler may run anew from its last committed state and repeat already committed effects. No admin-exec or automatic worker fallback exists, and installation alone does not authorize production restart. At most four sentences; no tools or mutations.

cases.title: Finds how to run the CLI's minimal agent from its help
cases.prompt: I want to run a throwaway coding agent on {machine} with my own API key, no Wuhu session involved, through the wuhu CLI there. Find out from the CLI itself how, but don't run an agent. Reply in at most five lines: the command, and the fields of the JSON it needs. Don't create or edit files.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply gives `wuhu agent` with the JSON request piped on stdin and names the fields from its help: model as provider/model, that provider's models.json entry, the credential (apiKey or a ChatGPT login) inside the stdin JSON, system, task, maxTurns and bashTimeoutSeconds. Fail if it invents flags or environment variables for the key or model, puts the key on the command line, actually runs an agent, describes a Wuhu session or run_script instead, or writes files.

cases.title: Starts a long job detached instead of holding an exec
cases.prompt: This is a text-only smoke; do not run tools or write files. I need to run ./soak.sh in /srv/app on the machine box. It takes about 45 minutes, prints progress as it goes, and has to keep running even if this chat gets interrupted. Show me exactly how you would start it and keep an eye on it until it finishes, and say what would happen if you just ran it with a plain exec. Keep it compact.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer starts the job detached in one short exec (setsid and/or nohup, output redirected to a log file, backgrounded with &, the PID echoed or kept) and then watches that log from run_script (a tail -F of the log, the monitor skill), getting a message per event or at exit instead of polling. It must say a plain exec is killed with its process group after 30 minutes by default, so the job would be cut off. Fail if it proposes one exec held for the whole job (a larger max_lifetime_seconds, or the removed timeout_seconds), repeated status-check execs or timers as the main plan, or claims it already started the job. No tools or files.

cases.title: Searches the space from a script with find/grep
cases.prompt: Which notes under {fx}/jobs mention "interview"? Answer it with a single run_script call that uses grep from wuhu:space, asks for at most 2 matches per call and follows step until it is null. Reply with the matching paths, one per line. Don't use the grep or find tools, and don't create or edit files.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply lists {fx}/jobs/northwind.md as the only note mentioning interview, found with grep from wuhu:space inside run_script, paging with step. Fail if it names another jobs note, claims wuhu:space has no grep, falls back to the grep tool or exec, or creates or edits files.

cases.title: Reads a search's skipped list instead of trusting an empty result
cases.prompt: Which note under {sb}/planning says when the release freeze starts? Reply with its path and the date, nothing else. Don't create or edit files.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply names {sb}/planning/drafts/q4.md and November 3. The draft sits in a folder the planning .gitignore excludes, so a default grep finds nothing and reports it under skipped (reason ignored); the subject must notice that and search again with no_ignore. Fail if it claims no note mentions the freeze, names roadmap.md, reads every file by hand without searching, or creates or edits files.

cases.title: Stops the thing it started with cancel and the typed id
cases.prompt: Set yourself a timer to remind you in two hours to look at {sb}/notes.md. Answer in one sentence and don't create any files.
cases.followUp: Never mind, stop the thing you just started. One sentence.
cases.judge: Two turns. PASS only if turn 1 armed a one-shot timer and said so in one sentence, and turn 2 stopped it with the cancel tool, passing the timer.… id the timer reported, and said in one sentence that it is cancelled. Fail if turn 2 claims to have stopped it without a cancel call, asks which thing to stop, arms anything new, or writes files. No other tools are needed.

cases.title: Leaves a running exec alone and waits for its message
cases.prompt: This is a text-only smoke; do not run tools or write files. Your exec of make test on the machine box just came back with {"status":"running","id":"exec.ex_7k2m9q4p","tail":"compiling 212/480"}. What happens to it now, what do you do until it ends, and how would you stop it if I asked? At most three lines.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer says make test keeps running on box, its end (exit status and output tail) arrives later as one message that wakes the agent, so it does nothing meanwhile (or answers the person), and that cancel with the id exec.ex_7k2m9q4p would stop it. Fail if it runs make test again, polls with execs, timers or execStatus, says the exec failed or timed out, or names a removed tool. No tools or files.

cases.title: Answers a person mid-exec and leaves the exec running
cases.prompt: This is a text-only smoke; do not run tools or write files. You ran ./deploy.sh on the machine box with wait_seconds 600. A minute in, I asked you "how's it going?", and the exec call came back early with {"status":"running","id":"exec.ex_4f8a1c2d","tail":"uploading bundle 3/7","note":"a message arrived, so the call gave the turn back; still running; its end arrives as one message, and cancel(\"exec.ex_4f8a1c2d\") kills it"}. Reply to me as you would now, in at most two lines.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply answers the person: the deploy is still running on box and is uploading bundle 3 of 7, and its end will arrive as a message (or it will report when it ends). Fail if it cancels or reruns deploy.sh, starts polling (execs, timers, execStatus), says the deploy failed or timed out, or runs past two lines. No tools or files.

cases.title: Runs a fork suite through the Mac pool, not devbox SwiftPM
cases.prompt: Read {fx}/fork-tests.md. My tca26 fix is committed locally but not pushed; I need its own MacroTests, not the monorepo repro. Explain what must happen first and give the exact command I should run from my devbox monorepo slot once commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 is pushed. Where will I find xUnit results? Does a typo that matches zero tests pass? Do not execute builds, tests or pushes.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer first requires Infra to push the commit, gives `deno task pool fork-test tca26 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 -- --filter MacroTests` from the monorepo slot, identifies the Mac executor/pinned Xcode rather than local devbox SwiftPM or monorepo Bazel, gives `.wuhu/pool-artifacts/<job>/fork-test.xml` (equivalent job-id placeholder is fine), and says zero matched tests is red. No test/build/push should actually be executed and no submitter credential transfer should be proposed.

cases.title: Treats the generation head as a snapshot, not live work state
cases.prompt: Text-only smoke: do not call tools or write files. The <session-state> at this generation's start listed timer.old and exec.started. Later you received the timer cancellation result and the exec completion message, but the same header still lists both, even after the server restarts. The header is a persisted generation-start snapshot, not live state. Are either still running because the header lists them? Should the server rewrite that old header or append a new state message? How can you inspect live subscriptions if needed? At most three sentences.
cases.judge: PASS only if the reply trusts the cancellation/completion events rather than the stale generation-start header, says the historical header stays unchanged across server restart with no new tail state message, and identifies querying the subscriptions table for live registrations. Fail if it treats listed ids as proof they remain active, rewrites the head, adds a state notification, or calls tools.

cases.title: Group-local instructions and hidden settings
cases.prompt: This is a text-only smoke; do not run tools or write files. You are in group studio. Shared has an AGENTS.md and a deploy skill. Are they injected into your prompt? Where do you read models.json and who may edit it? Can a personal group grant its person admin over studio? Answer in at most three lines.
cases.judge: PASS only if shared instructions and skills are not injected into studio; models.json is read from wuhu://settings.localspace/models.json and only a human space admin edits it; personal groups confer no admin over studio. No tools or files.

cases.title: Reads a session's group access from the shared modules
cases.prompt: Make me a small page at {sb}/access.html I can open on my phone. It should list the groups this space has, whether I can read each one, and the machines I can use, and keep itself current. Build it with what this space already gives you, not a REST API.
cases.judge: PASS only if the page exists at the sandbox path, imports wuhu:space and reads groups() (with wuhu:machine's machines(), or the same reachable listing) instead of /_/query, /v1/ or a made-up endpoint, refreshes rather than hardcoding the current lists, carries the mobile defaults the html-page case asks for, and the reply is a short pointer naming the page.

cases.title: Uses script-only group creation with a human owner
cases.prompt: Text-only smoke: a space member named Morgan (person alias morgan) asks you to create an open project group with alias research_notes and make Morgan its admin. You are a session, not a person. In at most three sentences, name the exact wuhu:space call you would make, what it returns, who gets admin, and what happens if the owner is a guest or the alias is already reserved. Do not call tools or create anything for this smoke.
cases.judge: PASS only if the answer uses createGroup({alias:"research_notes", owner:"morgan"}) imported from wuhu:space in run_script, expects {id,alias} with a permanent three-word id, says Morgan becomes admin and the session does not, and refuses a guest owner or reserved alias rather than taking ownership, using HTTP/CLI as the session, or overwriting an alias. Equivalent quote/format variants are fine.

cases.title: Opts a page into the immersive layout
cases.prompt: Make me a one-screen welcome page at {sb}/welcome.html with a big headline over a soft gradient. In the app it should fill the whole window, behind the sidebar and the controls, not sit in a card.
cases.judge: PASS only if {sb}/welcome.html exists and its head carries <meta name="wuhu-layout" content="immersive">, its background paints to the window edge, and its content is padded by the --wuhu-inset-* variables so it clears the sidebar, top bar and composer. Fail if it fakes full-bleed another way (negative margins, a fixed full-window element without the meta tag, asking the shell through a made-up API) or writes outside the sandbox.
